title: CLAY CITY VILLAGE BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Clay City Village Board held another busy session at its regular monthly meeting Tuesday evening.

Mayor Mike Delonshaw called the meeting to order, and it quickly took an unusual turn over a dispute about the bills.  Trustees made a motion to approve the past meeting minutes and the bills.  Trustee Sue Lindeman said she would second the motion only if it excluded payment for SCIRPDC (South Central Illinois Regional Planning & Development Commission).  No one caught the change in language, and the board approved the motion on a 3-2 vote.  Attorney Barry Bright stepped in with a procedural question.  He asked what her motion was, and Lindeman said she wanted the SCIRPDC bill left out.  Bright then called for a separate motion on the SCIRPDC payment, which the board approved 4-1 with Lindeman voting no.  The board then approved the rest of the bills unanimously.  Lindeman said she objected to the payment because trustees had not learned about the mayor’s decision to approve spending on a grant application for demolition costs of dilapidated buildings around town.  She said she did not oppose the expense itself, only the way the village handled it.

Mayor Delonshaw asked if anyone had questions about the sheriff’s report.  Sheriff Andy Myers, who attended the meeting, reported that a new deputy has joined the staff and is now training at the police academy.  After graduation, the deputy will begin serving Clay County.  Myers added that the new hire will let the Clay City School Resource Officer focus fully on Clay City Schools under the terms of the recently approved agreement.

Trustees next returned to the ongoing effort to help Ali Hilderbrand open a new beauty shop.  After earlier plans to locate west of Casey’s, the village and Hilderbrand agreed on a new arrangement.  The village will offer two lots at 201 and 209 South Main Street for five thousand dollars and will handle utility setup.  Hilderbrand will install a building at her own expense for her new business, Ali’s Beauty Barn.  Her mother, Amanda Hostettler noted that Hilderbrand has less than ninety days before she must leave her current location in Flora.  Hostettler asked whether the contract was ready so work could begin.  Attorney Bright said he had prepared the contract for board approval.  Hostettler also said the site needed rock for a rear parking area.  The village agreed to provide 400 pounds of rock and to include that in the contract.  Bright said a few more changes were needed.  He expected the mayor to sign the agreement Wednesday morning, after which the village must approve an ordinance to finalize it.  Hilderbrand and Hostettler will then review the document with their attorney.

The board continued its discussion on whether to lease a new backhoe or buy the one it already leases, depending on availability of an extended warranty.  Members tabled the item again while they seek the best option.

Trustees also revived the search for a new pickup truck for the utility department.  After collecting quotes from area dealerships for several weeks, the board accepted an offer from Dan Hecht Chevrolet in Effingham.  Members voted unanimously to buy a 2027 Chevy 1500 Crew Cab that includes a snow plow mount.  The price is $47,340, with delivery expected in October.

Someone’s interest in building a new home in Sunset Acres has now become reality.  Danielle Lister reached an agreement with the village to install a new single-family home at the corner of Kelly and Eleventh Streets.  In exchange, the village will provide the lot and utility hookups.  Attorney Bright will prepare an ordinance to formalize the deal at the next meeting.

Village trustees agreed to apply for the latest OSLAD grant before the application window closes.  They learned their previous request was reportedly rejected because it lacked ADA-approved playground equipment.  That earlier application included sidewalks around the Clay City Park, a handicapped parking space near the ballfield, and other grant-friendly items.  The new application must stay under $600,000.  Mayor Delonshaw asked Brandon Bridges of Charleston Engineering whether he could reduce some of the sidewalk work to make room for the playground equipment.  Bridges said he could.  Delonshaw and Bright noted the application must go through SCIRPDC.  Bridges said he can finish it by the August 31 deadline.

Village Attorney Barry Bright reported that Utility Gas Management, the village’s natural gas agent, is seeking a three-year contract extension that includes a price increase.  The last time the company requested a thirty-three percent rise in its management fee, the board found the long-term cost acceptable.  This time the firm is asking for a flat fee of two hundred fifty dollars a month.  Bright said the increase remains acceptable when viewed overall and recommended approval.  The board agreed to the three-year extension.

As the meeting neared its end, Utilities Superintendent Sean Sullen reported that a natural gas valve needs repair at a cost of nine hundred dollars.  The alternative would be a new unit costing several thousand dollars.  Trustees raised no objection.  Sullen also said the department’s chop saw is broken and workers have been renting one as needed.  Discussion also touched on the nuisance property at South Fourth Street and Washington Street Southwest and efforts to see it cleaned up.  Attorney Bright said he has spoken with the owner; the property is being sold, and results should appear in the near future.  With all business finished, the meeting adjourned.

title: S.U.R.E. SYMPOSIUM
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department is collaborating with the Coalition Against Drug Abuse of Clay County, the Clay County Board, SIU School of Medicine, and Birth to Five Illinois to bring the second Substance Use Resource & Education Symposium or S.U.R.E Symposium to Clay County on August 11th.  Registration will begin at 8:30 am at the Oil Belt Christian Service Camp.

The goal of the S.U.R.E. Symposium is to bring together local agencies, experts, and community members to provide a safe space to learn about substance abuse prevention, recovery, and what happens after.

Speakers will be Liesl Wingert from the SIU School of Medicine, Shelly Kuhns, with Gentle Care Consultants, Andy Greer with the Gateway Foundation, Clay County States Attorney Phil Givens, and Clay County Sheriff’s Sgt Elam Lewis.

Lunch will be provided to the first 200 who register, and continuing education units are pending.  Register by going to tinyurl.com/SURE2026 or use the QR code on the health department’s website.  This years symposium registration is being covered by the Clay County Board Opioid Settlement.

Representatives from the Health Department will be on the ReVue today at 2 pm to discuss the event.

title: ISP KIOSK IN EFFINGHAM
full_story:
The Illinois State Police (ISP) opened its newest Firearm Owners Identification (FOID) kiosk, providing real-time, in-person assistance to Illinoisans who need help with their Firearm Owner’s Identification (FOID) cards and Concealed Carry Licenses (CCL).  The newest kiosk, located at the ISP Troop 9 headquarters in Effingham, was created to assist individuals experiencing difficulties with the online FOID and CCL website, or those without online access.

The Effingham kiosk will be available Monday through Friday, from 8:00 am to 12 pm and from 1:00 pm to 4:30 pm.

ISP currently offers other kiosks in Springfield and Du Quoin. Additional kiosks in Collinsville and Lockport are expected to reopen this fall.

These kiosks will provide, assistance with submitting name or address changes, renewals, and new applications online.  Taking a photo and uploading it to the application, assistance with correcting rejected applications, submitting firearm disposition records (FDRs), and surrendering FOID/CCL cards when required.

Due to the extended time it takes for kiosk representatives to assist people with submitting applications online, customers may be asked to return at a different time.  New and current FOID and CCL card holders may continue to use the online ISP Firearms Services website to apply, update, and renew their cards and licenses.

title: SALES TAX HOLIDAY COMING
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Revenue announced a State Sales Tax Holiday for certain school clothing and school-related items for back-to-school expenses from Friday, through Sunday, August 16th.

The state sales tax holiday is a ten-day period during which consumers can purchase certain clothing and school-related items and pay sales tax at a reduced rate.  The state’s portion of sales tax due throughout the holiday is reduced by 5% from 6.25% to 1.25%.  Items include traditional supplies such as markers and pencils, notebooks and folders and other classroom items, as well as many clothing purchases.  Clothing items, including shoes, that cost less than $125 will qualify for a lower sales tax rate, while there will be no price limit on school supplies.

The last time the state approved such a program was in 2022, the last time JB Pritzker ran for reelection.

The sales tax holiday starts on Friday and ends on August 16th.

title: COUNTRY FINANCIAL AT FAIR
full_story:
Last week, COUNTRY Financial Representatives Lisa Erbacher, Lisa Cash and staff were at the Clay County Fair and sponsored an activation called Tourniquet in Every Tractor.  Approximately 70 farmers at the fair received tourniquets and training from Collin Moseley, ESDA First Responder, and Captain Sam Larch from the Clay County Ambulance/Rescue Department.

The “Tourniquet in Every Tractor” program is a community farm-safety initiative co-sponsored by Country Financial, local county farm bureaus, and regional emergency medical/ambulance services.  The program provides farmers with free, life-saving trauma tourniquets and hands-on medical training to treat severe, uncontrollable bleeding from machinery accidents during high-risk seasons like harvest.

Pictured: Captain Sam Larch, Clay County Hospital EMT & Rescue; Lisa Cash, COUNTRY Financial Representative; Allison Czyzewski, COUNTRY Financial; Collin Mosely, ESDA and First Responder

title: ACTION REQUEST
full_story:
Illinois Farm Bureau issued an action request Tuesday urging members to ask Senate Agriculture Committee member Dick Durbin, to support a proposed farm bill that includes language authorizing year-round nationwide E15.

The committee is scheduled to mark up the bill Thursday before the Senate adjourns for its August recess.

Senate Ag Chair John Boozman released the updated farm bill 2.0 titled the Agricultural Act of 2026 Friday.  The legislation updates key farm bill programs that have not been revised since Congress last passed a comprehensive farm bill in 2018.  Farmers have been without the certainty of modernized farm bill policy since the 2018 bill first expired in 2023.

The bill provides important support for farm families including improved access to credit, expanded investments in specialty crops, increased transparency in fertilizer markets and enhanced research and conservation programs.

The House passed its version of a farm bill in August, which did not include year-round E15 authorization.  However, the House passed a separate bill authorizing the sale of year-round E15.

Both the House and Senate bills build upon last year’s reconciliation bill that invested $66 billion in farm programs and strengthened parts of the farm safety net, but reconciliation rules left major farm bill titles unfinished.

The action request will remain open until a vote comes before the Senate Ag Committee.  IFB members can access the action request link at bit.ly/4w9O690.

title: SUNDAY NIGHT ACCIDENT
full_story:
The Jefferson County Sheriff’s Department reports a man fearing deportation ran from the scene of a single car wreck on the Dix-Irvington Road south of Centralia Sunday night.

Police say Raul Vazquez was located west of the accident, and with the help of a translator, it was determined he was driving under the influence of alcohol, fell asleep, traveled through a bean field, and ramped his vehicle through a pond before it overturned.  He had a blood alcohol level of .154, nearly twice the legal level of intoxication.

Vazquez was transported to Good Samaritan Hospital due to his injuries and the severity of the crash.  He was cited for aggravated DUI, leaving the scene of a crash, improper lane usage, and no valid drivers license.  The owner of the bean field also requested charges in connection with damage to his field.

The crash was reported at almost 11 Sunday night.  Since the crash occurred on the Jefferson Fire and Centralia Fire Protection District line, both departments responded to assist.

title: LAKE LAND STEM NIGHT
full_story:
Lake Land College is hosting its first-ever community STEM night at the Effingham Technology Center tonight, giving community members of all ages the chance to enjoy hands-on activities with high-tech educational equipment.

The Lake Land College community STEM night will be from 5 to 7 pm this evening.  The event will focus on video game development, with in-depth instruction and demonstration led by Lake Land College staff.

All attendees will also get to practice coding and design their very own video games.  Attendees can also bring a flash drive to save and take home their games.

The event will take place in the Lake Land College Innovation Center on the first floor of the Effingham Technology Center.  Registration is not required to attend the event.

For more information about Lake Land College community STEM night, contact Innovation Center Assistant Tiffany Maillet-Gibson at 217-234-5328 or [email protected].

title: IPRB SUMMER PROGRAM
full_story:
Thirty-six Illinois educators completed the 16th IPRB Summer Teachers Program June 23rd through 26th.  The program included an oil lifecycle field trip, including a drill site, two active production sites, an oil storage and transportation facility located at the Patoka tank farm and a CountryMark refinery tour.

Teachers also participated in learning stations and watched presentations by industry professionals and academics covering Illinois geology, wellsite geology, hydraulic fracturing, drilling and producing, oil and gas careers, land and legal aspects of the industry, coring, drill stem testing, drilling mud, seismic mapping, subsurface fluid migration and much more.  Teachers participated in oil-and-gas focused educational workshops featuring classroom lessons and activities included in Illinois State Board of Education-approved curriculum, in addition to taking home oil-and-gas focused classroom activity kits.
